transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-25
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Leo (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Ethan (BrightScale CTO), Priya (BrightScale SRE), Liam (BrightScale ML)
Shared links: https://redwood.app/s/brightscale-pilot, RED-3421 incident ticket (internal)

[00:00] Ava: hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call, um, just to follow up on the reliability incident last week - RED-3421 - we want to align on root cause and next steps
[00:28] Ethan: thanks Ava, yes we had a large spike during our batch scoring window, saw a mix of 504 timeouts and 502/503 5xxs, latency spiked to 3.4s for tail. it's blocking our nightly job
[00:46] Priya: and for us the rate limits were weird - we hit a 429 cluster level limit then clients started retrying in tight loops, which I think made things worse
[01:07] Leo: right, on our side the traces show a combo of sustained queueing on the serving nodes and some RPC connection resets, looks like the autoscaler didn't spin up fast enough because the spike was short but intense
[01:30] Liam: also noticed KV cache misses during the spike, curiosity if prefix caching warmed up; we saw a lot of cold-cache penalties
[01:45] Ava: ok good context. quick question - are you on the hosted pilot or dedicated pool for this run?
[01:52] Ethan: hosted for now, we asked for dedicated but haven't cut over yet - timeline slipped to next week
[02:05] Maya: that matters - dedicated gives more predictable throughput and isolates noisy neighbors; but we still need client retry/backoff tuned
[02:20] Priya: can you explain what you saw on your end Leo? any 5xx root cause hints?
[02:29] Leo: sure - looking at the logs we saw a cascade: initial 429s at the API gateway, clients retried with no jitter, gateway started returning 503 from the upstream when queues hit capacity, then some downstream worker OOMs for a small subset. we have stack traces attached in the RED-3421 ticket
[02:56] Ethan: hmm we definitely have a tight retry policy in our glue service, it's currently 3 immediate retries, no jitter - oops
[03:08] Ava: yeah that's a pattern we've seen - immediate retries amplify the spike. easiest win is add exponential backoff + jitter, cap concurrency in your client, and consider a circuit breaker on 5xxs
[03:30] Priya: what's the recommended backoff window? like base 200ms, factor 2, max 5s?
[03:39] Leo: that seems reasonable. I'd do base 100-200ms with full jitter, max about 5-10s. also on server we can add a soft queue cap and graceful 429s with Retry-After header so clients back off instead of thrashing
[03:59] Liam: are there any Redwood SDK knobs we should flip? we use the JS/Go clients
[04:06] Ava: yes - we have client-side retry middleware in the SDKs, but customers sometimes override. we'll include a snippet in the follow-up. Leo: will you paste the recommended config?
[04:17] Leo: yes I'll put a sample for JS/Go and the server-side rate limit headers in the ticket
[04:25] Ethan: can we also get the exact timeline of the autoscaler events? we want to map the spike to scale events
[04:33] Maya: sure, Redwood will extract scaler logs and share; that will show why nodes didn't come up quickly (cold start vs scale delta)
[04:43] Priya: during that window we also saw memory pressure, any suggestion on model batch sizes or quant settings?
[04:52] Leo: from the model side you can reduce max_batch_size and lower concurrency, or try a quantized variant - e.g., redwood-v2-meduim-quant (note: transcriber sometimes writes meduim) - those reduce mem pressure at some perf tradeoff
[05:10] Ethan: ah ok, we were running max_batch 64, maybe that's too high for our instance type
[05:16] Leo: for hosted non-dedicated instances, keep batch sizes conservative, maybe 8-16, and rely on continuous batching in the runtime. for dedicated GPUs you can bump batch sizes because you get more capacity
[05:34] Liam: about caching - is there a way to warm prefix cache during ramp?
[05:40] Leo: yes, we recommend a warm-up job to prime KV cache for known prefixes, and persistent cache between requests when using dedicated. we'll share a script sample
[05:50] Priya: you mentioned some upstream 5xxs were due to OOMs - do we have which pods were impacted?
[05:58] Leo: attached in logs - a small percentage of worker pods hit OOM on heavy requests that had very long sequences; we can add request size guarding to reject too-large calls early
[06:12] Ethan: what about rate limiting? we saw gateway-level limits and then a per-customer throttle kick in - how do those interplay?
[06:22] Ava: gateway limits protect the control plane; per-customer throttles are separate. in practice if you hit both you can get surprising 429 patterns. We'll map those thresholds in the follow-up doc so you can tune the client to stay under the soft threshold during ramping
[06:40] Priya: do you have recommended strategies for bursty workloads? our nightly jobs burst for 15-20 minutes then quiet
[06:48] Leo: for bursty patterns we recommend a short burst window on dedicated with pre-provisioned burst capacity, or if hosted, use a staged ramp where your job spreads requests over a few more minutes, combined with client jitter and retries
[07:05] Maya: operationally, we'll also propose an escalation path and an SLA matrix for production vs pilot flows; that will help prioritize Dedicated procurement if you need the tail latency guarantees
[07:18] Ethan: what about metrics - what should we be watching on our side to detect the pattern earlier?
[07:25] Leo: watch 5xx rate, 429 rate, queue depth, p99 latency, and backend pod memory RSS. instrument client-side retry counts too, that often spikes before server-side errors
[07:40] Priya: ok we'll add those to our dashboard - stack: Prometheus/Grafana on our side
[07:47] Ava: quick note: we saw some mis-attributed spans in traces - sometimes operator labels come through as 'Speaker 1' or 'red wood' in the logs - disregard those typos in the ticket, actual traces are attached
[07:59] Ethan: ha ok noted.
[08:05] Liam: about testing - can Redwood run a controlled load test on a dedicated node so we can compare with our hosted runs?
[08:14] Maya: yes we can schedule a 3-hour benchmark on a dedicated pool, run the same request mix you used. that'll show whether dedicated removes the noisy neighbor effect
[08:26] Ethan: perfect, please do that. also can you capture kernel-level metrics? we saw some ephemeral spikes at the infra layer
[08:33] Leo: yes, we'll collect system metrics and eBPF traces if needed; we'll include those in the RED-3421 package
[08:44] Priya: one other ask - can we get the exact Retry-After and rate threshold values so we can match them in our client?
[08:50] Ava: yes, Leo will include that in the ticket and the SDK sample
[08:56] Ethan: timeline ask - we'd like resolution before we go live with the nightly pipeline in two weeks
[09:02] Maya: agree, we'll prioritize. immediate wins first (client retry config), medium (run dedicated benchmark), and long (dedicated procurement if needed)
[09:15] Ava: ok let's go through immediate actions - Leo, you'll paste SDK config and server headers; Maya will pull scaler logs; I'll send consolidated notes
[09:25] Leo: I'll also run a small synthetic test (10 RPS for 30 minutes) with your request shape to validate the retry/backoff impact
[09:33] Priya: we'll share our exact request traces and the spike timestamps from our telemetry by EOD tomorrow
[09:40] Ethan: do you have any note about SSO/permissions for the dedicated trial? our security team wants to review network diagram
[09:47] Maya: yup we'll share the VPC diagram and KMS integration doc; that's on the next steps list
[09:54] Liam: small nit - sometimes the SDK error messages say 'model unavailable' even when it's a rate limit; is there a mapping table?
[10:02] Leo: yes the SDK maps some upstream statuses to friendly errors; we'll include a mapping table so you can interpret 5xx vs rate limit vs retryable transient errors
[10:12] Ethan: great. any blockers on Redwood side for the dedicated benchmark?
[10:17] Maya: none, just need your approval on the time window and request shapes - we'll schedule and run it next week
[10:24] Ava: ok last thing, recap: immediate change - client retry/backoff + jitter, cap concurrency; Redwood action - share logs, scaler events, SDK samples, run dedicated benchmark; BrightScale action - share telemetry, approve benchmark window, apply client change in staging
[10:44] Priya: sounds good, thanks all
[10:47] Ethan: appreciate the quick turnaround
[10:49] Ava: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the packet and a calendar invite for the benchmark review
[10:55] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (red wood => Redwood, meduim => medium), some speaker tags auto-labeled; see RED-3421 for raw logs and attachments.
